question: Why did US unemployment spike in 2020?
summary: US unemployment rose in 2020: 3.6% (2019-12) -> 14.8% (2020-04 peak), +11.2 pts; 2018 average 3.9%. The evidence is consistent with these drivers: (1) leisure & hospitality employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak; (2) initial jobless claims rose during the run-up to the 2020 peak; (3) industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak.
supported: Initial jobless claims rose during the run-up to the 2020 peak
Total payroll employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
Leisure & hospitality employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
Construction employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
Manufacturing employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
Industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak

H1: Initial jobless claims rose during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H2: Total payroll employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H3: Leisure & hospitality employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H4: Construction employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H5: Manufacturing employment fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H6: Industrial production fell during the run-up to the 2020 peak
H7: The federal funds rate rose during the run-up to the 2020 peak

reference: Unemployment jumped to 14.7% in April 2020 as COVID-19 shutdowns cut 20.5M payroll jobs, with leisure and hospitality down 7.7M (BLS Employment Situation, April 2020).
